index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure presents a hierarchical taxonomy tree for mechanical metamaterials, structured as a top-down flowchart. At the apex is a single rectangular node labeled 'Metamaterials', which branches into two main categories: 'Mechanical metamaterials' and 'Other types'. The 'Other types' branch further splits into five parallel rectangular nodes on the right side: 'Acoustic metamaterials', 'Thermal metamaterials', 'Electronical metamaterials', 'Optical metamaterials', and 'Transport metamaterials', each connected by a horizontal arrow from the parent node. The primary focus of the diagram is the 'Mechanical metamaterials' branch, which divides into two subcategories: 'Porous metamaterials' and 'Composite metamaterials'.

Under 'Porous metamaterials', three subtypes are listed horizontally: 'Close cell', 'Open cell', and 'Mixed cells'. The 'Open cell' node further branches into 'Periodic', 'Gradient', and 'Hybrid'. The 'Periodic' node then subdivides into 'TPMS', 'Honeycomb', and 'Lattice'. The 'TPMS' node leads to 'Cubic' and 'Rhombohedral'; 'Cubic' further branches to 'SC' and 'BCC', with 'BCC' leading to 'Kelvin'. 'Honeycomb' connects to 'Hexagonal', which then branches to 'FCC' and 'Simple'; 'FCC' further splits into 'Octet' and 'Diamond'. 'Lattice' connects to 'Tetragonal', 'Orthorhombic', 'Monoclinic', and 'Triclinic'. 'Tetragonal' leads to 'HCP', 'Orthorhombic' to 'Triangular', and 'Triclinic' to 'Kagome'.

The 'Composite metamaterials' branch includes four subtypes: 'Particle-based', 'Fiber-based', 'Tablet-based', and '3D'. These further divide into 'Hybrid', 'Hierarchical', and 'Stochastic'. The 'Stochastic' node branches into 'Weaire-Phelan Structure', 'Voronoi Foam', and 'Polyhedral Foam'. All nodes are represented as white rectangular boxes with black borders and black text. Connections between nodes are indicated by solid black arrows pointing downward or to the right, indicating hierarchical relationships. The layout is strictly vertical and left-to-right, with clear branching and sub-branching to show classification levels. The diagram is clean, with no colors or additional visual embellishments beyond the basic box-and-arrow structure. The caption indicates this taxonomy is used for internal inductive bias extraction in a computational context.
